Test_Description: Verify GPIO register default reset values and write-read data integrity across GPIO pad registers GP0_GPIO_8 through GP0_GPIO_27. The test writes 6 different data patterns (0xFFFFFFFF, 0xAAAAAAAA, 0x55555555, 0xF5F5F5F5, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xFFFF0000) and reads back with mask verification.
Test_Procedure: Step 1: Read all GPIO registers and compare against default_value_array (reset value check). Step 2: For each of 6 data patterns - write pattern with write_mask to each register then read back with read_mask and verify against expected value. Step 3: Expected value = (written_data AND read_mask AND write_mask) OR (NOT write_mask AND read_mask AND default_value). Step 4: Count mismatches in def_fail_cnt and wr_fail_cnt.
Expected_Result: All register default values match expected reset values. All write-read operations return expected masked values for all 6 data patterns.

Test_Description: Verify GPIO negative-edge triggered interrupt functionality for all 32 GPIO pads (GPIO_8 to GPIO_39). Each pad is configured for negative-edge detection and the interrupt is triggered by driving the pad from high to low. The ISR validates pin status and group interrupt status then clears the interrupt.
Registers_Tested: MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 to GP0_GPIO_39, MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1, MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1, MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1, MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1, MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1
Test_Procedure: Step 1: Enable GIC IRQ (87 for GPIO0 or 88 for GPIO1). Step 2: Enable sysreg interrupt for GPIO. Step 3: Configure all 32 GPIO pads with negedge interrupt enable (bit20=1 bit18=1 bit16=1). Step 4: For each pad i (0-31): clear raw status write interrupt enable for pad i set int_pend=1 drive pad high then low (negedge). Step 5: Wait for ISR (timeout 5000 cycles). Step 6: In ISR - verify pin din==0 verify group interrupt status bit is set clear interrupt via iclr verify group status cleared clear sysreg status and GIC IRQ.
Expected_Result: Each of the 32 GPIO pads generates a negative-edge interrupt successfully. ISR fires within timeout. Pin status shows din=0 after negedge. Group interrupt status correctly reflects the active pad. Interrupt clears successfully.
Fail_Criteria: test_err > 0 OR timeout on any pad → finish(test_err)

Test_Description: Verify GPIO positive-edge triggered interrupt functionality for all 32 GPIO pads simultaneously. All pads are configured for posedge interrupt detection. The test drives all pads from low to high to generate a rising edge and validates group interrupt assertion and clearing in the ISR.
Registers_Tested: MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 to GP0_GPIO_39, MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1, MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1, MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1-4, MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1, MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1
Test_Procedure: Step 1: Enable GIC IRQ (87 for GPIO0 or 88 for GPIO1). Step 2: Enable sysreg interrupt for GPIO. Step 3: Configure all 32 GPIO pads with posedge interrupt enable (bit17=1 via write 0x00020000). Step 4: Set GPIO IO control groups 1-4 for input mode (doe=1 0x000000FF). Step 5: Enable all group interrupts (GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1 = 0xFFFFFFFF). Step 6: For each iteration i (0-31): drive all pads low (0x00000000) set int_pend=1 drive all pads high (0xFFFFFFFF) to create posedge. Step 7: Wait for ISR (timeout 2000 cycles). Step 8: In ISR - verify group interrupt status is non-zero clear all per-pin raw status via iclr (bit16) verify group status cleared to 0 clear sysreg status and GIC IRQ re-enable group interrupt.
Expected_Result: All 32 iterations produce a positive-edge interrupt. ISR fires within timeout for each iteration. Group interrupt status is correctly asserted on rising edge. All interrupts clear successfully after servicing. Sysreg status clears properly.
